questions.question: When weight is loaded high in a vehicle, what happens?

options.text: The vehicle is more likely to tip over.
Items are more likely to fall down.
It becomes harder to unload the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo loaded high in a vehicle increases the risk of a rollover. Load cargo with weight spread evenly and as low as possible.

questions.question: Where should the center of gravity be in a trailer?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
At the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep the weight of cargo as low as possible in a vehicle. A high center of gravity increases the risk of a rollover.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Use a different method each time to focus on different parts.
Use the same method each time to make sure you check everything.
Do them once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the same method each time to make sure you check everything.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way before every drive. Following the same steps helps you remember to check everything and prevents you from missing anything.

questions.question: What do wheel chocks do on flat surfaces?

options.text: They stop a parked vehicle from rolling.
They make it easier for a parked vehicle to roll.
They should only be used on the front driver's side tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stop a parked vehicle from rolling.
questions.explanation: When you cannot use a parking brake, wheel chocks can hold a parked vehicle in place on a level surface.

questions.question: A posted speed limit for cars may affect buses differently. Which is true?

options.text: It is usually safe for buses.
It may be too fast for buses.
It may be too slow for buses.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may be too fast for buses.
questions.explanation: Speed limits posted for cars may be safe for cars but too fast for buses, especially on curves. Be extra careful when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: How far does an air brake truck need to stop from 55 mph in ideal conditions?

options.text: 300 feet
100 feet
450 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 450 feet
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and actual braking distance. An air brake truck traveling at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely in ideal conditions.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most newer heavy trucks use?

options.text: Single air brakes
Dual air brakes
Triple air brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brakes
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: What stops air from leaking out if the air compressor has a problem?

options.text: Slack adjuster
One-way check valve
Tractor protection valve

questions.correctAnswerText: One-way check valve
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve sits between the air compressor and the main air tank. It prevents air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?

options.text: Water
Cardboard
Brake fluid

questions.correctAnswerText: Water
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes over time. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When is it acceptable to fuel a bus with passengers on board?

options.text: Only at night.
Only on trips longer than 100 miles.
Only if it cannot be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if it cannot be avoided.
questions.explanation: Never fuel a bus with passengers on board unless absolutely necessary. Never refuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: How often should you inspect cargo during a trip?

options.text: Another driver should inspect it.
Only after the trip is finished.
Every time you take a break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you take a break.
questions.explanation: Inspect your cargo and how it is secured every time you take a break. Check it at least every 150 miles.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to operate?

options.text: Compressed air
Outside air
Non-compressed air

questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air
questions.explanation: Air brakes on large commercial vehicles use compressed air to work.

questions.question: What is the safe maximum air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?

options.text: 3 psi in one minute.
6 psi in one minute.
8 psi in one minute.

questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should lose no more than 3 psi of air pressure in one minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: What happens in a dual air brake system if one system loses pressure?

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one system loses too much pressure. If this happens while driving, you should stop and park as soon as possible.

questions.question: What is the purpose of blocking a load?

options.text: It is only used for liquid cargo.
It helps keep the load from moving.
It is dangerous and should never be done.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps keep the load from moving.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from shifting during transport.

questions.question: What should a driver do when the bus arrives at a destination?

options.text: Rest.
Tell passengers to take their belongings when they exit.
Only make announcements after passengers start to exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell passengers to take their belongings when they exit.
questions.explanation: When arriving at a destination, remind passengers to take their belongings before exiting. Make this announcement before the bus stops completely.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Look both ways, but do not stop.
Stop and get out to look for a train.
Stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks and look both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks and look both ways.
questions.explanation: Stop your bus 15 to 50 feet before the railroad tracks. Look and listen for trains. Only proceed when you are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: When can you rely on front wheel braking?

options.text: On dry roads only.
Under all conditions.
Under all conditions except snow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under all conditions.
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works well in all road conditions, even on ice. Front wheel skids are unlikely.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure drops below 55 psi in an air brake system?

options.text: The warning light should turn on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.
The front lights should flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must turn on before air pressure drops below 55 psi. If it does not work during an inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located?

options.text: In the fifth wheel.
Inside a brake drum.
In the landing gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inside a brake drum.
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are located inside the brake drum.
